followUp.mechanism: Two layers, both by design and both identical for the old and the conformant path: (1) the tier 1 derivation is decline-only since the anti-zombie cut, so a stamped parcel with a ring stores {status: declined, declineReason: atom_path_pending}; (2) the serve route nulls envelope and forces facetCoverage.envelope false on the wire. The served null is the strip, not a bake omission; the stored row is the authoritative record and carries the declined object exactly as the old bake wrote it.
rejected: Claim maps an input under a different name / geometry precondition: rejected because the stored rows carry acreage.method shoelace-wgs84 and parcelJoin.state joined, so the ring reached computeTier1Envelope and it took the stamped branch (atom_path_pending); a missing ring produces envelope null, a missing district produces no-zoning-stamp. The same-fixture test (n.envelope toEqual o.envelope) passes.

District rule lookup key (bastrop_city_tx underscore vs bastrop-city-tx hyphen): rejected because the tier 1 path performs no rule lookup at all; the jurisdiction key is carried on the decline, not consumed. The hyphen/underscore difference is real but belongs to the atom-chain adapter, a separate producer.
Coverage flag computed before the derivation: rejected because facetCoverage.envelope is hardcoded false after the derivation (anti-zombie) and forced false again at serve; ordering cannot change it.
followUp.decision: The old tier 1 bake did NOT carry a derived envelope; the bake is left as is (branch B). The reader gets its envelope from the atom-chain BFF, and the brief never gets one from anywhere (see routing).
followUp.routing: Inspect card and fact sheet: the browser reads PE_FACETS_PROXY_BASE=/api/spine/property-atoms (fact-sheet-resolver.ts:1543); with PROPERTY_ATOM_PATH=1 (live, per the header) the BFF serves facets.envelope from the atom chain and merges the bake baseFacts (mergeBakedBaseFacts); setbacksFact/envelopeValue read it and facetsNeedLiveEnvelopeDerive (status ok + setbacks) triggers the live buildable-envelope POST for geometry. The bake envelope never reaches these surfaces: when the chain is empty the BFF substitutes honestAtomPendingResponse (declined atom_path_pending) which renders as pending. Brief (R1): the cortex route POST research/brief reads the bake only (routes/propertyExplorer.ts:560-587: loadBakedNodeFacetSnapshot, then buildR1Brief(snapshot.facets, tier2, {envelopeBriefRefusal})); the served envelope is null after the strip, extractEnvelopeBriefRefusal yields declined-in-bake: atom_path_pending, buildR1Brief emits section data null + refusal, and brief-view-model deriveSetbacksEnvelope renders the operator line (no envelope was derived for this parcel snapshot). That line has been true for every baked parcel since 2026-07-23 regardless of shape. Routing options for the planner: (a) the R1 route composes the setbacks section from the same atom-chain adapter the BFF uses (server-side read of the chain), (b) PropertyBriefPanel composes the setbacks section from the sheet it already holds (the sheet carries the atom-chain envelope), (c) un-strip at serve, which reverses WDLL 3.7 and is not recommended.
followUp.bareNull: One bare-null case remains in both bakes: a parcel with no ring stores envelope null (old-bake parity). The branch-A shape (facetCoverage.envelope: declined + provenance.envelopeDecline) was not applied because branch B says leave the bake; it is a small follow-on if wanted.
